notes: Colour clock 3.579545 MHz; 228 clocks x 262 lines = 59736 clocks per frame = 19912 CPU cycles (76 per line). Frame rate = 3579545 / 59736 = about 59.92 Hz (derived; broadcast NTSC is 59.94 and Gopher2600 uses a 15734.26 Hz line rate, giving about 60.05).
Layout from the Stella guide: 3 lines VSYNC + 37 VBLANK + 192 picture + 30 overscan = 262. Gopher2600 uses the same split in its NTSC specification.

The guide adds the programming convention for timers: a 37-line vertical blank is 2812 CPU cycles and a 30-line overscan 2280 cycles; the matching TIM64T values depend on the cycles the surrounding code spends, so derive them from your own code.

The Stella guide groups the 16 hues in pairs with rough names: 0-1 grey to gold, 2-3 orange, 4-5 pink to purple, 6-7 purple-blue to blue, 8-9 blue to light blue, A-B turquoise to green-blue, C-D green to yellow-green, E-F orange-green to light orange. The colour actually shown varies between TVs and emulator palettes.

standards.palette: 128 entries (16 hues x 8 luminances); unverified: common PAL palettes show hues 0, 1, 14 and 15 as grey
notes: Colour clock about 3.546894 MHz; 228 clocks x 312 lines = 71136 clocks per frame = 23712 CPU cycles; frame rate about 49.86 Hz (derived; Gopher2600 uses a 15625 Hz line rate, giving 50.08).
Layout: 3 VSYNC + 45 VBLANK + 228 picture + 36 overscan = 312 (the Stella guide lists the vertical blank as 48 lines including VSYNC). Gopher2600 uses the same split.
Vertical blank of 45 lines = 3420 cycles and overscan of 36 lines = 2736 cycles; pick the TIM64T value from your own cycle count.
PAL hue numbers do not mean the same as NTSC ones, so an NTSC colour table must be remapped. The Stella guide only says NTSC and PAL share the black-and-white description.
Slower clock lowers the pitch of audio and 50 Hz slows frame-based game speed by about 17% (Stella guide).
PAL colour clock with the NTSC line count (262 lines): NTSC timing code works unchanged, the PAL palette applies and the frame rate is 3546894 / 59736 = about 59.38 Hz (derived).
Stella names the format PAL60; its NTSC counterpart for a 312-line signal is NTSC50. Not every PAL TV accepts a 60 Hz signal.

standards.palette: 8 colours selected by COLUxx bits 3-1 (hue bits 7-4 and bit 0 are ignored)
notes: SECAM consoles use PAL timing (312 lines, 50 Hz). The Stella guide says SECAM takes the PAL software but the console's colour/B&W switch is hardwired to B&W, so the software's B&W (luminance) table selects one of 8 fixed colours: luminance bits 3-1 = 0 black, 1 blue, 2 red, 3 magenta, 4 green, 5 cyan, 6 yellow, 7 white (the guide lists them by luminance value 0, 2, 4 ... E).
Silence on SECAM must be made with AUDVx = 0 rather than AUDCx = 0 (Stella guide).
Stella also has the SECAM60 format for a 262-line signal.

The TIA has no register that reports the TV standard, so software cannot ask whether it runs on NTSC or PAL. Common solutions: separate ROMs per region, a start-up menu choice, or a software heuristic. The colour/B&W switch (SWCHB bit 3) is only a console switch.

Frame structure: count the lines of VSYNC, VBLANK, picture and overscan from constants defined per standard (for example with DASM IFCONST/IF blocks). Timers are a convenient way to run the vertical blank and overscan: write TIM64T, do the work, wait for INTIM = 0 and finish with WSYNC.
Use one colour table per standard; do not hard-code hue numbers.

Timing in CPU cycles per line (76) is identical in NTSC and PAL; only the number of lines and the frame time change. Game speed tied to frame rate needs a scale factor (Stella guide: PAL is about 17% slower per frame).
A PAL cart usually shows more lines (228 against 192); a kernel written for 192 lines leaves black borders on PAL unless extended.
Stella's '-format' option accepts NTSC, PAL, SECAM, NTSC50, PAL60, SECAM60 and AUTO (the cartridge type is '-bs'). Gopher2600 uses '-tv' with AUTO, NTSC, PAL, PAL60, PAL-M and SECAM.
The colour/B&W switch can be used to choose a luminance-only palette when it reads 0.
